body.text: A commercial airliner made of cardboard to cut costs

nodes.title: Pressurized skin holds together
nodes.statement: Corrugated cardboard fuselage skin carries the pressurization load with the required safety margin.
nodes.rationale: Pressurized fuselage is a pressure vessel. If cardboard cannot carry hoop tension with aviation safety margin, the hull bursts in flight.

check.description: Hoop stress from pressurization must stay within allowable divided by safety factor.

nodes.title: Wings carry flight loads
nodes.statement: Cardboard wing structure carries the limit maneuver load without collapsing or breaking.
nodes.rationale: Wings must support the whole aircraft weight multiplied by maneuver load. Cardboard buckles and crushes easily, so spar failure would mean loss of the wing.

check.description: Wing root bending stress at limit load must stay within allowable divided by safety factor.

nodes.title: Cardboard survives getting wet
nodes.statement: Cardboard keeps enough strength after long exposure to humidity, rain and condensation.
nodes.rationale: Airliners sit in rain, ingest condensation, and cruise through humid air. Cardboard softens dramatically when wet, so dry lab strength is not enough.

check.description: Wet strength after moisture exposure must still exceed the stress required in service.

nodes.title: Fire rules can be met
nodes.statement: Cardboard airframe meets aviation fire resistance and burn-through certification rules.
nodes.rationale: Aviation rules require fire blocking and burn-through protection to allow evacuation. Untreated cellulose ignites easily and cannot be certified without fundamentally changing the material.

check.description: Time to burn through the cardboard barrier must meet the minimum required for evacuation.

nodes.title: Airframe lasts service life
nodes.statement: Cardboard fuselage survives the full service life of pressurization cycles without fatigue failure.
nodes.rationale: An airliner pressurizes on every flight for decades. Paper fibers creep, delaminate and grow cracks under repeated loading, so short packaging life does not transfer.

check.description: Demonstrated pressurization cycle life of cardboard must reach the required service life.

nodes.title: Cardboard actually cuts cost
nodes.statement: Frequent replacement and upkeep of cardboard still leaves total cost below a metal airliner.
nodes.rationale: Cheap per sheet does not mean cheap per lifetime. If the hull must be rebuilt constantly and grounded for inspection, replacement labor and downtime erase material savings.

check.description: Lifetime hull replacement cost for cardboard must stay below the metal hull it replaces.

body.summary: Read as primary load-bearing fuselage and wings made of corrugated packaging cardboard to lower cost, not just cardboard interior panels or trim. The concept fails on strength, moisture, fire, fatigue and lifetime cost.

nodes.title: Thickness and margin suffice
nodes.statement: The chosen wall thickness keeps pressure tension below the safe strength with margin.
nodes.rationale: This is the arithmetic heart of the parent: given pressure, geometry, material and margin, the wall either holds or bursts.

check.description: Hoop stress from pressure load must stay within allowable divided by safety factor.

nodes.title: Cardboard hoop strength
nodes.statement: Cardboard keeps its assumed pulling strength in the damp air of a pressurized cabin.
nodes.rationale: Corrugated board is paper fibers with starch glue; humidity and creep sharply lower tensile capacity, so the dry catalog value may not apply in service.

nodes.title: Cabin pressure load
nodes.statement: Pressure difference at cruise stays within the level of a normal airliner.
nodes.rationale: Airliners pressurize to roughly 75 kPa cabin at 10 km altitude, giving about 50-60 kPa difference; if higher differential or pressure spikes occur the load rises.

nodes.title: Hoop stress law
nodes.statement: Skin pulling force follows the thin-walled pressure vessel law.
nodes.rationale: Cutting a thin cylinder in half shows internal pressure must be balanced by wall tension, giving stress proportional to pressure times radius over thickness.

body.summary: The burst claim rests on the pressure load, the hoop-stress law, the cardboard strength in humidity, and the thickness-plus-margin calculation, which already fails on the assumed numbers.
